statement: When IRIS refuses the prepared path as unsupported, the cursor tries the written-in path, then %SQL.Statement; any other error raises at once.
After a successful statement the row count is -1 (not known), never the number changed; only a no-row statement reports 0.
Every Cypher query has a SQL-path answer; a query the native executor does not support (or declines) is answered by the SQL path exactly as with the native executor off
Python builds the native plan and IRIS runs it; the native executor never parses Cypher text
The privilege holds iff %All is among the caller's roles, or the login or any of its roles holds it on the table or its whole schema; a column-only privilege does not count
Public routes are matched on the exact path; a longer or different path needs the key
A server route is governed by strict mode only when it calls a guarded engine method; a route that runs its own SQL is not refused
Strict mode applies to an engine whenever the ledger is strict, however old the engine; an engine that first checked before the ledger classes existed is not left unguarded
The same node ID in two graphs is two distinct nodes; labels, properties and edges of one never count for, merge into or are changed through the other.
An edge's two endpoints are nodes of the edge's own graph; no writer can create an edge whose endpoint exists only in another graph.

delete_node / bulk_delete_nodes with graph omitted (not None) delete each ID from the one graph that holds it, a holder being a graph with a node row or an edge row naming the ID; with None they delete from the default graph.
Native index key: the default graph is the number 0; a named graph is its (NUL-stripped) name; no named graph's key equals 0.
Ledger key: the default graph is $Char(1); a named graph is its name; no named graph's key equals $Char(1).
No code converts one store's key into another store's key (or back to a name and on); each store's key comes from the name.

A key of one store used on the other matches only the same named graph or nothing; the default graph's key in one store matches no key of the other, so a misused default key reads nothing and its writes are invisible to readers.
GraphKey is the only code that derives a graph key or SQL spelling; no other module computes one inline.
A lookup with a key or graph name that has no content answers empty; it never falls back to the default graph or every graph.
Once any named graph holds an edge, every snapshot reader refuses or switches to the default graph's scoped index; none answers over all graphs merged.
MERGE without USE GRAPH matches and creates only in the default graph; ON MATCH changes only the default graph's node.
Complete bodies are dispatched in the order received; a queued body is handled before the next transport read
A 5.x proposal with a range is met at its highest minor up to 5.4 (5.8 range 4 gives 5.4; 5.8 alone or 5.6-5.8 refused)
A failed RUN answers FAILURE with a status code and the failure text; RESET then a new RUN succeeds
Every revision (genesis, changeset, adoption, redaction audit) gets seq = previous head + 1; no gap, including after a caller's rollback
A relationship reference must give exactly one of statement ID, (source, predicate, target, graph) tuple, or earlier-create reference; both or neither is refused at the builder
With auto-stubs, each stub op precedes its relationship and shifts positions; the returned reference names the shifted position
Ops apply in order; two writes of one property record (absent->1) and (1->2) and the property shows the last value
The first failing op stops the commit; no revision, record or content change of the changeset remains
More ops than max_ops refuses ChangesetTooLargeError carrying the limit; exactly max_ops commits

A text field over its column limit (message/source 4,000; actor/correlation/key 256; actor type 32) is refused as LedgerInconsistencyError after apply: nothing kept, nothing counted, hook sees inconsistent

A written, replayed or counted-refusal commit inside a caller's transaction holds the counter row to transaction end; meanwhile another connection's refused commit is not counted and a strict-mode count made elsewhere is lost
With the counter row held, the competing lock-timeout refusal arrives after about 40 s (30 s head wait + 10 s row wait); with only the head held, after 30 s
An uncounted nested refusal (e.g. inconsistent) holds the head but not the counter row; the competing lock-timeout is counted and the count survives the caller's rollback

After the caller's own nested commit times out, it holds the counter row without the head; another connection's valid commit then fails LedgerInconsistencyError after ~10 s, writing nothing, until the caller's transaction ends
A replayed (keyed retry) commit must not re-apply its post-commit properties; as built the pin re-applies them (F-1101)
Two concurrent commits with the same key and fingerprint produce one revision; the other replays
Node records carry no graph; relationship records carry the relationship's graph
Every record keeps its ordinal position; no writer reorders or removes record slots (redaction tombstones in place)
An object source is stored as compact sorted-key JSON and the source filter matches that exact text; a plain-text source is silently dropped
get_revision, diff, reconstruct and export refuse RedactionInProgressError while a redaction is unfinished, before looking up the ID
A full page returns its last seq as the cursor (also when final); a short or empty page returns none
None omits a filter; '' is a supplied filter
limit 0 returns empty; negative limit is refused by IRIS
Every acquired cursor is closed exactly once; a failed open closes none
Required: change-then-delete-then-recreate in range keeps the range-start value; as built the snapshot holds the value at deletion and the range prior is lost (bug-led-101)
A record that does not belong to the target (including another tenant's record in the same revision) stays byte-identical; only the target's records change.

Current behaviour: while strict mode stays on, a target whose graph still has node rows cannot be erased through the engine and its redaction is refused (target_live); the erase-then-redact sequence needs strict mode off.
A record outside the target graph never belongs to the target; with no prefix every record of the target graph belongs; with a prefix only records whose IDs begin with the match string do.

A relationship delete or detach delete inside a tenant's revision writes delete records for the relationship's reifier nodes with the reifier's own ID and the default graph; unless the reifier ID begins with the tenant's prefix, neither the tenant's graph target nor its prefix target tombstones them.

With a prefix, a create/delete relationship (or temporal-edge) record of the target graph belongs to the target iff its source or target ID begins with the match string; an unparsable tuple is unknown.
A qualifier record belongs to the target when its statement's relationship does (known from this run's redacting set or the statement endpoints); otherwise it is unknown and left in clear.

For a tenant with its own graph, the graph target plus the tenant prefix in the default graph together tombstone all of the tenant's records; either target alone leaves records in clear (node records, or the graph's relationship records).
Two calls are the same redaction (resume rather than refusal) exactly when graph and match string are equal; acme and acme| are one target.

For the whole default graph (no prefix) a node row live in any graph must refuse the redaction; as built only default-graph rows are counted, so named-graph node records are tombstoned while the node is live.
A later commit with a redacted key is refused (IdempotencyRedactedError) before the head check and before apply; nothing is written.
A redaction of a different target is refused with nothing changed while another is unfinished; as built two runs started before either tombstones both run.
First enable fixes max_ops and recon_bound and sets strict; set_strict switches strict later
Before the first enable: commit, redact, head, verify, set_strict refuse LedgerNotEnabledError; history is empty
Disabling mid-redaction keeps the marker; the next batch refuses LedgerDisabledError; after enable the same redaction resumes
Re-enable takes strict from the call (default off); set_strict while disabled is reset
Each server-reached commit emits exactly one event per registered hook; client-side refusals emit none
A tables-only entity is reported with its attributes; a history-only entity is one deletion entry whose adoption also removes its attributes
A label or non-reserved property row makes a node exist in the tables view; an orphan property (e.g. post-commit) is reported as an unrecorded node with that property
Tables drop rows with temporal JSON true; replay drops statements with temporal text 'true'
Intended: tables and replay leave out the same relationships; a caller-given temporal 'true' is an ordinary qualifier
The BFS walk, its SQL fallback, the ends-only walk and the shortest-path routines each answer from one graph's entries; edges in another graph change no answer
Without the declared index, Cypher writes, store_edge and the store's write_edges change rows but not the adjacency index, which stays stale until a rebuild
Every change to ^KG out-edge and in-edge entries is made by the one adjacency module (Graph.KG.Adjacency); no other component writes them
bulk_create_nodes and bulk_create_edges, having dropped the indexes for a large batch, rebuild them before returning, on success and on failure
After an in-transaction bulk_load_session the loading engine reports pending_sync True until sync(), even after the caller rolls back, while another engine or process reports False
For MatchEdges a graph argument of '', NULL, 0, '0' or none selects the default graph alone, and no value selects every graph; SQL '' arrives as character 0 and is read as empty
With IVG_EDGESCAN=1 a hop from a node named by id with no USE GRAPH or USE GRAPH '' is answered through the scan; a named graph or the flag unset uses the edge rows

No adjacency index is declared (no DDL, drop or backfill) while the callback classes or the schema's procedure class are not compiled, the edge key column is missing, or either table lacks the graph column; setup skips with a reason and a later setup declares them
A reader stores its count only when its no-wait exclusive probe of the graph's writer lock succeeded and the node's generation did not move while it counted
WarmAll fills the all-predicate entry and each predicate entry of each source and returns the number of sources filled, not entries; target-only nodes are not sources
WarmAll sets the whole-graph stamp only when every visited source filled and the token stayed equal; otherwise it removes the stamp and readers use per-source checks

Today khop2_count_fast with a type answers, while the two-hop statistics are current, the sum of the middle nodes' out-degrees (counting a start reached back and a target once per middle node), and after any write the walked count
Only the time-index component reads or writes the temporal stores; every other component goes through its operations
A delete recomputes the bucket's count, sum, extremes and sketch from the surviving edges and lowers the event counter by one, removing it at zero
A write rolled back by its caller leaves its count, sum and event counter, while its edge, extremes and sketch are undone
While a triple of a structural predicate has any timestamp in a graph, that graph has its structural edge (row), so SQL, Cypher MATCH, edge counts and traversal see it
Under ledger strict mode a direct temporal write is not refused
A Native Reader is used only for PageRank, PPR, WCC, CDLP or subgraph; any other algorithm is answered by its Owner
A Native Reader is used only when the proof record lists the algorithm; an unlisted algorithm is answered by its Owner
A Native Reader is used only when the loaded library's Reader Revision for it is at or above the proof record's minimum; below it or unreported, the Owner answers
A Native Reader is used only for a default-graph call; a named-graph call is answered by its Owner
A Native Reader is used only in namespace USER; in any other namespace the Owner answers (the library would read USER's graph)
Routing that depends on availability reads engine.capabilities/status() or falls back explicitly; it never reads the store's static capabilities() catalogue as availability
A cached answer is served only while its graph's content is unchanged; no stale answer is ever returned
Only answers that depend on the adjacency index alone are cached; an answer that also depends on node rows or properties is either completed fresh on each call or not cached
WCC and CDLP cache labels for adjacency nodes only; every public call reads the current edgeless nodes and adds each missing one with its own label, even on a hit
Global PageRank's cache key holds the node table's row count and largest row ID, damping and iteration count; any difference misses
An unreadable node token makes PageRank read the edgeless list before lookup and key on it; a failed token is not treated as a known empty node set, while an empty table reads 0:0
PageRank's adapter removes self-loop-only nodes from the edgeless list; a remaining true isolate forces the Owner, a self-loop-only list does not
The registry keeps one current identity per (table, graph); a forced re-claim replaces it and no earlier identity is retained
store_embedding naming a model never changes a recorded identity; it writes to (or creates) that model's own route
Two concurrent first writers create one route; both use the recorded width
Re-creating an orphaned route reuses the table only when its column width equals the requested width; otherwise refused
Unplaceable documents and edge vectors go to their own quarantine tables; no API places them
Placement succeeds only when the route exists with equal width and dtype and the node is in the graph; otherwise refused and the row stays
A failed index write rolls back only its own level; the caller's earlier writes in its open transaction survive
IVF scope is known only to the building engine object; a fresh engine or IRISGraphOperators reads HNSW instead, so answers differ

The ^NKG-reading procedures (Cypher CALL ivg.betweenness/closeness/eigenvector/leiden/triangleCount/scc/kcore and the SQL kg_* functions) raise, naming the Python method to use, exactly when a graph other than the default holds an edge; otherwise they answer.
Every algorithm answer has a row for every node of the graph read, including nodes with no edge; only betweenness (score>0 nodes) and walks/subgraphs (what they reach) are exempt.
A whole-number string ('2') or float (2.0) option value is taken as that integer; a non-whole value is refused.
Global PageRank reads the default graph only; named-graph nodes and edges do not enter it.
Defaults damping 0.85 and 20 iterations; the Owner runs exactly the iteration count, while the Arno reader may stop earlier once converged.
Seeds are deduplicated; a seed that is not a node of the graph contributes nothing; unreached nodes are listed at 0.0.
CDLP starts with own IDs; each round every node simultaneously takes the most frequent neighbor label (either direction, self-loops not voting), ties to the least label.
Nodes carry properties and labels by default; vectors only when requested.
out/in score the directed graph, both the undirected graph; max_hops=k counts only pairs within k hops.
gamma 1.0 optimizes modularity; other gamma values use CPM.
Rows are {id, community, size} with community 0 the largest; top_k cuts rows, possibly through a community.
A seed with no out-edge answers itself only; a seed that is no node answers nothing.
khop walks the default graph only; named graphs' edges never change its answer.
A graph walk whose answer exceeds one IRIS string raises; a khop read of the same size answers.
An edge is kept only when its confidence qualifier is at least the threshold; an edge without it is dropped.
Equal endpoints answer length 0; an empty endpoint answers no path.
Edge cost is its stored weight; zero, negative or missing weight costs 1.
The public procedure refuses a negative hop limit; the native search treats one as unbounded.
The public procedure refuses an empty/missing endpoint; the native search answers no path for one.

A Cypher variable-length pattern returns one row per path (openCypher multiplicity) on the native and SQL paths: over a->x->b, a->y->b, a->b, *1..2 gives b three times and x, y once; *2..2 gives b twice; *0..1 includes a
execute_bfs lists each node other than the start exactly once, at its least depth, ordered by (depth, id); a cap k keeps the first k rows of that order (0 = all)
When Arno is not chosen the ObjectScript walk answers; the SQL walk answers only when the ObjectScript walk raises or walks no edge
The ends-only walk (VarLength.Ends) never uses a relationship twice in one path, so a cycle can make the start an end; an undirected walk does not come back over the edge it arrived by
A failed Cypher write inside a caller transaction takes back only its own changes; the caller's earlier work stays pending
A write clause inside a CALL { } body is either carried out or the whole query is refused with nothing written; it is never skipped silently

The engine decides once (cached) whether Prop_Set exists, from the dictionary; an unreadable dictionary is taken as deployed, so where the function is missing the write fails instead of keeping the old type
DELETE r removes only that relationship; its endpoint nodes remain
Under read_only=True a write in any statement of a ;-separated text refuses the whole text before its first statement runs
A gds.* call accepts after YIELD only a WHERE and a RETURN of yielded names; other clauses are refused
Only a condition evaluating to true keeps a row; a comparison with null drops it
As built, a bare YIELD label AS l keeps result column 'label'; with RETURN l the column is 'l'
Unsupported WHERE expressions and missing parameters raise only when the producer has rows; an empty producer returns no rows without error
Each aggregate is computed from exactly the rows reaching its stage, partitioned by the grouping keys; every row contributes to its own group's accumulator only
SUM over typed numbers is an integer iff every contributor is an integer; one float contributor makes it a float even when the total is whole
collect() keeps each element's type; a nested list or map is collected as a list/map, distinct from a string spelling it
SQL path: grouping keys, count(DISTINCT) and WITH DISTINCT merge a stored number with its spelling (key reads as one of them); RETURN DISTINCT and collect(DISTINCT) keep them apart
SQL path: stored 1 and 1.0 are one value for grouping and count(DISTINCT) but two for RETURN DISTINCT; over a held list RETURN DISTINCT and UNION make them one row
Over a held list, grouping and count(DISTINCT) merge 1 with true, 0 with false and a list with the string spelling its JSON, while RETURN DISTINCT keeps them apart; 'true' and true stay two groups
A WHERE inside OPTIONAL MATCH removes only matches; the incoming row is never dropped and the query does not fail
A leading grouped OPTIONAL MATCH with no match answers sum null; its other aggregates follow the rule
The -94 refusal follows negation-normal form: NOT(OR with earlier) runs; NOT(arith over earlier) and NOT(AND with earlier) are refused
A property of an unbound node is null at the four readers and both drivers, also through WITH; collect() of the unbound node is []
An unbound node answers b_id null, b_labels and b_props '[]' at execute_cypher, /api/cypher and tx/commit; Bolt answers null
As built, CALL { } importing an UNWIND variable, or a node into a body without MATCH, fails; importing a node into a body that matches from it works
DISTINCT over nodes compares identity; over a property compares values
As built, a numeric string, a boolean and a whole float parameter are used as counts; a non-numeric string raises ValueError; null is reported as not provided
Wherever a literal is allowed, a parameter of the same value and type gives the same answer, at execute_cypher, Bolt and HTTP
Driver 5.3.2: UNWIND $list, $l[$i] and $l[$s..$e] fail; 5.4.1 runs them; WITH $list AS l works under both
UNION answers the branches' rows without duplicates; UNION ALL keeps duplicates
As built, a relationship in a UNION ALL branch answers its JSON text; alone it answers a map
As built, a literal list in a UNION branch answers JSON text; alone it answers a list
WITH coalesce(...) AS x RETURN x answers a stored number or boolean as text under both drivers; RETURN coalesce(...) is typed
A relationship whole float 1.0 equals 1 but not true; a node double 1.0 equals both
A string literal or parameter spelling a node's stored number equals it; an integer literal or parameter matches only the number
A node property orders against a number only when stored as a number; text and booleans drop the row
Over a held list RETURN ... ORDER BY sorts booleans among numbers; after WITH it follows the key
A missing node property is null in WHERE: =, <>, IN and NOT of each drop the row; IS NULL keeps it
String predicates test a node number through its canonical text (12 STARTS WITH '1'; 0.95 as '.95') while RETURN reads a number
Node IN compares text: '1' IN [1] (though = is false), 1 IN ['1']; '01' and '1.0' match neither
Non-canonical numeric spellings stay text; True is text; 1 and 0 are integers, not booleans
As built, a bare run-time boolean as a condition fails the query; b = true and NOT b work
As built, a simple CASE with a property/run-time test takes a WHEN of another kind with matching text; literal tests and same-kind WHENs follow the rule
As built percentileDisc takes index floor((n - 1) p): p 0.6 gives 20 and 0.9 gives 30 over 10..40; p 0.95 over 1..10 gives 9
As built trim() in a result or SET removes spaces only (tabs and line breaks kept; rtrim keeps a line break)
As built otherwise a number or boolean answers as text (UNWIND [7] AS x RETURN coalesce(x, 1) gives '7'; coalesce(null, 1) gives '1')
load_networkx writes one item at a time; on failure the items already written remain
import_rdf commits per batch; a failure keeps earlier batches
Blank lines are ignored; malformed/non-object JSON, unknown kinds and nodes without IDs are logged and counted skipped, and later lines are still processed
A writer exception stops the import with no counts; earlier writes remain (no caller transaction)
Record kind: explicit kind wins over type; type node|rel used when kind is absent
A non-null property becomes a literal triple; NULL emits nothing
Property keys pass through only for http/https/urn, otherwise urn:ivg:prop/<key>
Two unqualified parallel rows give one triple; two qualified rows keep separate blank envelopes
A registered repository is projected into its own named graph fhir:<namespace>:<package>, never the default graph; a FHIR graph call without a graph id refuses
The graph holds exactly one node per live resource, keyed by its FHIR key and labelled with its resource type; deleted resources have no node
Codes and most properties are not copied into the graph; readers read them live from the repository
Registering a repository names its graph deterministically (fhir:<namespace>:<package>); registering again updates the same graph's settings
Scheduling creates a Task Manager task when the graph has none and otherwise updates its own task, so a graph has one sync task
Status reports the graph's node, reference-edge and compartment-edge counts, pending changes past the watermarks, last sync and rebuild, last error and task id
An existing object is reused only when its class is Graph.KG.FHIRGraphSyncTask, its namespace is current and its Settings' GraphId is this graph; otherwise it is foreign
The public interval must be an integer of at least 60 or None (retain the registered interval); explicit 0, 59 or a non-integer refuses with nothing changed
Task save/delete happens before the registry update; a failed save/delete stops before SQL, while a failed later SQL update keeps the saved or deleted task with the old registry
A task run whose sync answers ok or busy succeeds; an error reply, a thrown SyncOnce or an unparsable reply fails
A sync applies exactly the repository changes past each of the two watermarks (new resources; later versions and deletes), in batches of keys
An event's optional graph field writes the node and edge into that named graph; without it they go to the default graph; an invalid name refuses
Inside a caller's open transaction an engine write is nested in it; the caller's commit keeps it and the caller's rollback removes it, however the caller opened the transaction.
A failed engine write inside a caller transaction takes back only its own level; the caller's earlier work stays pending.

purge_before and set_temporal_structural run on the engine's own Native API connection when the engine knows its credentials (from_connect) and are durable whatever the caller does; on the caller's connection they follow the caller.
A node's own graph key overrides the call's graph keyword; an explicit None graph is the default graph; an absent key uses the keyword.
Before inserting parents, properties of incoming IDs that have no node row in that graph (orphans) are removed; offered values replace them.
None-valued properties are not written; id defaults to the node ID when absent; an explicit None id writes no id.
delete_node removes the node, its labels and properties and every edge incident to it in its graph; other nodes stay.
deleted counts nodes removed by successful calls; failed counts every requested ID of a raising call, existing or not.
A node delete can finish before its reifier cleanup raises; the batch then counts as failed (false result) although the nodes are gone.
A bare node is returned; an absent ID with no child rows is omitted and get_node returns None.
Stored properties id and labels are returned as p_id and p_labels; the structural id and labels fields are kept.
A failed database read raises; no empty node is fabricated.
get_nodes_by_property and get_node_ids_by_property match val against the stored text: '7' finds number 7 and string '7'; 'true' finds a stored true.
As built, get_property_values/get_property_pairs return a stored boolean true as the string 'true' while get_node returns True.
set_edge_weight updates the default graph's edge; the same triple in another graph keeps its weight.
A reifier is linked to exactly one edge row; a second link of the same reifier is refused.
In a multigraph, CREATE of an existing triple adds another edge with its own key; each stays distinct in rows and adjacency.
As built, create_edge/store_edge in a multigraph do not add a parallel edge (they guard on ekey 0); only Cypher CREATE does.
Two equal parallel edges are two Cypher relationships; DISTINCT folds them to one.
Cypher DELETE r of one of two parallel edges leaves a bare leaf with the survivor's weight; reach stays and degree goes 2 -> 1.
A degree answer equals the count of the node's adjacency entries at the time asked; no maintained counter answers it.

As built, an undeclared (no model key) default-graph writer whose width and element type match is admitted into kg_NodeEmbeddings even when that table records a declared model; separate-route enforcement is not current behaviour
Two model keys match iff they are equal after trimming, lowercasing and collapsing runs of whitespace; no other rewriting (punctuation, hyphens, aliases) is applied
The registry's recorded width for a table follows the vector column's declared width (reconcile copies it); the registry never overrides a declared column width
Setup changes an empty column's declared width only when rewidth=True; without it the empty column at another width is refused
A query vector of another width than the route/column is never padded or truncated; it raises an error and no scores are returned
The width refusal is raised before any search statement runs, names the query width and the stored width, and compares against the route's recorded width or, when none, the column's declared width

No width check is made for a seed node ID, for a route and column with no declared width, or for an unparseable literal; IRIS then decides and an IRIS refusal is raised, never turned into an empty answer
A write naming a model key lands in that (graph, model)'s own route, and every reader of that pair reads it there; two declared models never share one table
A vector read for a (graph, model) with no route answers nothing, never another graph's, model's or table's vectors; the default pair (default graph, no model) reads the original tables
Searching an unrouted pair answers empty even with a wrong-width query; it is never a width error
Every route gets an HNSW index attempt; if refused, the route is still searched by full scan
The threshold is a WHERE predicate on the cosine expression with a second query-vector bind; the graph predicate is conjoined; ORDER BY follows
Each vector read and write is scoped to exactly one graph; an omitted graph means the default graph
The same node ID in two graphs holds two independent vectors; writing one leaves the other unchanged
A BM25 build indexes the nodes of exactly one graph; no graph named means the default graph
Cosine: score = cosine, distance = 1 - score; dot: score = dot product (largest first), distance = its negative; l2, l1, chebyshev: score = distance
vec_drop removes all vectors; a later search returns nothing
After a build, ivf_insert/ivf_delete change one node's entries; a rebuild replaces the index with the route's current vectors
Searching for an absent node or an unbuilt index answers no hit and no error; inserting into a missing index is refused
Plain text search (kg_TXT) never falls back to a BM25 index; BM25 is used only when selected explicitly
Scores are compared at 12 decimals; ties are ordered by IRIS subscript collation of IDs (canonical numbers first by value, then by character codes); the first k are answered
With f > 0 (schema 2), known query terms with df/N > f are skipped; with no fraction nothing is skipped
As built, a failed vector or graph leg is logged and dropped; it is absent from search_modes and the ranking can be incomplete
Engine kg_RRF_FUSE requires c; IRISGraphOperators and kg_RERANK default c to 60; kg_RERANK searches each leg 2 x top_n deep
Expansion follows only edges with confidence >= 1000 x min_confidence; an edge without confidence is not followed
A wrong-width query raises; a graph without vectors answers nothing
As built, the REST bodies check width before route lookup; an unrouted named graph expects 768 and refuses another width
A failed REST read raises with its SQL code; a missing privilege names the table
multi_vector_search fetches 2 x top_k rows per source and fuses by sum of weight/(rrf_k + rank); any other fusion value ranks by raw score ignoring weights
A failing source is logged and skipped; the answer can come from fewer sources; all failing answers nothing
The unit is set by the entry point (engine: seconds; TemporalIndexMS: milliseconds) and a bucket is five minutes in either unit.

The stored coordinate is derived from the raw caller timestamp, its normalization and the selected writer (single, Counts, prewrite fallback) and the per-item clock; equal resolved times give equal coordinates and different zero-time clock readings give different coordinates.
A numeric ts=0 short alias defers to a supplied long timestamp alias; text ts='0' keeps zero.
A direct write defaults to insert mode; an insert at occupied coordinates keeps the existing edge and reports a collision.
A positive explicit timestamp replayed after a completed write collides at its coordinate; the fallback reports one accepted call, inserts nothing and reports no collision.
A bucket-range purge returns the number of buckets in range that held statistics; a reversed range removes nothing and returns 0.
Today the Python reader raises ValueError for min, max, average and unknown metrics on an empty answer, while count answers 0.
A millisecond-class edge is counted by seconds whole-bucket counts, groups, velocity and distinct estimates but not by target reads, edge-by-edge reads or cut windows.
A registration change never blocks writers; a write in flight during registration may add a marked edge, which a later drop removes.
A source list returns the union of its sources' events, each once; an empty list returns nothing.
An omitted source filter reads every source; an explicit empty list reads none.
The server reads every source only with no source, list or prefix; a list of nothing or only empty strings reads nothing.
Each page is read live from the resume point of the previous page; the server keeps only that resume point between pages.
Only a page marked done ends the read; an empty page not marked done makes the reader ask for the next page.
Closing mid-read sends one close; a second close or a close after the end sends nothing; a closed reader yields nothing more.
A failed page raises after exactly one close; a failed open raises with nothing open.
Resolving a known hash returns its canonical text; an unknown hash returns ''.
Python purges retire bare nodes by default; ObjectScript purges only when asked.
A no-route row names no table, counts 0 and shows no index; a routed graph has no such row
Graph.KG.Service answers no request until an operator runs CreateWebApp; setup does not create the web application
The web-app role holds only read on the databases its routes read and EXECUTE on the routines its search routes call; it cannot write
Unrecorded, tables in one other schema, no name given: refused naming that schema; nothing recorded
Unrecorded, tables in several schemas, no name: refused, listing each schema with row counts; nothing recorded
Upgrade discards compiled Cypher plans built against the old names; none is reused
The current exporter's archive is consistent only when writers are quiet (an operator premise); a consistent snapshot under concurrent writers needs a verified snapshot or epoch protocol.
save_snapshot archives every graph of the namespace; no call archives one graph.
Configuration tables (FHIR registrations, SQL table mappings) match on primary key: replace writes the archive's row; merge keeps the live row.
An archive with another layout is refused before erase; an unstamped archive is accepted.
